mark.7.p1.b1.text: Then the Pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered around Jesus,

mark.7.p1.b2.text: They saw some of His disciples … with hands that were defiled—that is, unwashed.

mark.7.p2.b1.text: Now in holding to the tradition of the elders, the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat until they wash their hands ceremonially.

mark.7.p2.b2.text: And on returning from the market, they do not eat unless they wash.

mark.7.p2.b3.text: And there are many other traditions for them to observe, including the washing of cups, pitchers, kettles, and couches for dining.

mark.7.p3.b1.text: Why do Your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders? Instead, they eat with defiled hands.

mark.7.p3.b2.text: Isaiah prophesied correctly about you hypocrites,

mark.7.p3.b3.text: As it is written: These people honor Me with their lips, but their hearts are far from Me.

mark.7.p3.b4.text: They worship Me in vain; they teach as doctrine the precepts of men.

mark.7.p4.b1.text: You have disregarded the commandment of God to keep the tradition of men.

mark.7.p4.b2.text: You neatly set aside the command of God

mark.7.p5.b1.text: For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother’

mark.7.p5.b2.text: And ‘Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death.’

mark.7.p5.b3.text: But you say that if a man says to his father or mother, ‘Whatever you would have received from me is Corban’

mark.7.p5.b4.text: (that is, a gift devoted to God)

mark.7.p6.b1.text: He is no longer permitted to do anything for his father or mother.

mark.7.p6.b2.text: Thus you nullify the word of God by the tradition you have handed down.

mark.7.p6.b3.text: And you do so in many such matters.

mark.7.p7.b1.text: All of you, listen to Me and understand

mark.7.p7.b2.text: Nothing that enters a man from the outside can defile him;

mark.7.p7.b3.text: But the things that come out of a man, these are what defile him.

mark.7.p8.b1.text: Are you still so dull? … Do you not understand?

mark.7.p8.b2.text: Nothing that enters a man from the outside can defile him,

mark.7.p8.b3.text: Because it does not enter his heart, but it goes into the stomach and then is eliminated.

mark.7.p9.b1.text: What comes out of a man, that is what defiles him.

mark.7.p9.b2.text: For from within the hearts of men come evil thoughts, sexual immorality,

mark.7.p9.b3.text: Theft, murder, adultery, greed, wickedness, deceit, debauchery, envy, slander, arrogance, and foolishness.

mark.7.p9.b4.text: All these evils come from within, and these are what defile a man.

mark.7.p10.b1.text: Jesus left that place and went to the region of Tyre.

mark.7.p10.b2.text: Not wanting anyone to know He was there, He entered a house,

mark.7.p10.b3.text: But was unable to escape their notice.

mark.7.p11.b1.text: Instead, a woman whose little daughter had an unclean spirit

mark.7.p11.b2.text: Soon heard about Jesus, and she came and fell at His feet.

mark.7.p11.b3.text: Now she was a Greek woman of Syrophoenician origin,

mark.7.p11.b4.text: And she kept asking Jesus to drive the demon out of her daughter.

mark.7.p12.b1.text: First let the children have their fill,

mark.7.p12.b2.text: For it is not right to take the children’s bread and toss it to the dogs.

mark.7.p13.b2.text: Even the dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs.

mark.7.p14.b1.text: Because of this answer, you may go.

mark.7.p14.b2.text: The demon has left your daughter.

mark.7.p14.b3.text: And she went home and found her child lying on the bed, and the demon was gone.

mark.7.p15.b1.text: Then Jesus left the region of Tyre

mark.7.p15.b3.text: To the Sea of Galilee and into the region of the Decapolis.

mark.7.p16.b1.text: Some people brought to Him a man who was deaf and hardly able to speak,

mark.7.p16.b2.text: And they begged Jesus to place His hand on him.

mark.7.p16.b3.text: So Jesus took him aside privately, away from the crowd,

mark.7.p16.b4.text: And put His fingers into the man’s ears. Then He spit and touched the man’s tongue.

mark.7.p17.b3.text: Immediately the man’s ears were opened and his tongue was released,

mark.7.p17.b4.text: And he began to speak plainly.

mark.7.p18.b1.text: Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone.

mark.7.p18.b2.text: But the more He ordered them, the more widely they proclaimed it.

mark.7.p18.b3.text: He has done all things well!

mark.7.p18.b4.text: He makes even the deaf hear and the mute speak!
